description: Pinned inputs for the optional Qwen3-TTS GGUF engine (track qwen_gguf_engine_20260923). Consumed by scripts/build_qwen_gguf_runtime.py + scripts/lock_qwen_gguf_runtime.py (Task 1.2) to produce per-cell native packs, and by the GGUF model manifest (Task 3.2). Nothing here enters pyproject.toml, uv.lock, or the frozen base bundle.

sharedLibrary.note: Only QT_API symbols are exported; pipeline_*/backend_* stay hidden. The static qwen-core target is for the bundled tools, not ABI consumers.

deviceSelection.auto: unset: ggml_backend_init_best() picks the best GPU, else CPU
deviceSelection.note: There is no per-handle device or thread parameter in qt_init_params; CPU thread count is hardware_concurrency()/2 inside backend.h. Bounding threads further is a Phase 4/host-environment concern.

backendDiscovery.mechanism: GGML_BACKEND_DL=ON loads libggml-*.so modules dynamically at qt_init; ggml_backend_load_all() searches (1) compile-time GGML_BACKEND_DIR, (2) the host EXECUTABLE's directory, (3) the process cwd. It does NOT search the libqwen.so directory.
backendDiscovery.observed: qt_init fails with 'backend_init failed (no GGML backend available)' when libqwen.so is dlopened from a process whose exe dir and cwd lack the backend modules.
backendDiscovery.contract: The GGUF host subprocess MUST be spawned with cwd=<pack dir> (or the pack must set GGML_BACKEND_PATH to one explicit backend file, which forfeits CPU-ISA variant dispatch). The parent sets cwd at spawn; verified on linux-x64-cpu.

linux: libgomp.so.1 (OpenMP — needed by libggml-base and libggml-cpu-*; GCC runtime, must be shipped or floored)

runtime.cancelContract: qt_cancel_cb is polled during prompt processing AND at the top of every Talker decode step (~83 ms at 12.5 Hz); returning true ends synthesis with QT_STATUS_CANCELLED. on_chunk returning false is equivalent. Observed on linux-x64-cpu: terminal 'cancelled' with 0.2 ms latency, including a cancel requested mid-prefill (before any chunk).
runtime.streamingContract: on_chunk fires on the internal compute worker thread, never the caller; samples are mono float32 @ 24 kHz, valid only during the call (copy before return). First flush is one 12.5 Hz frame, chunk width doubles up to 8 frames, EOS/max_new flushes the remainder.
modeRules: speaker set but model_type != custom_voice: MODE_INVALID

ggufMetadataKeys.fileType: general.file_type (string) must equal the requested quantization
ggufMetadataKeys.languages: qwen3-tts.codec.language_names + language_ids — 12 entries on custom_voice (10 languages + beijing_dialect, sichuan_dialect), 10 entries on base (no dialect rows; confirmed via qt_language_name on the real model)

evidence.probeCommand:
cd <pack dir>  # backend modules resolve via process cwd
python scripts/spike/qwen_gguf_probe.py --profile customvoice --quantization Q8_0 --library <pack>\qwen.dll --talker <models>\qwen-talker-0.6b-customvoice-Q8_0.gguf --tokenizer <models>\qwen-tokenizer-12hz-Q8_0.gguf --speaker ryan --check-cancel --cell windows-x64-cpu --json-out docs/performance/evidence/qwen-gguf-windows-x64-cpu-customvoice-Q8_0.json (repeat per variant: --profile/--quantization and matching GGUF pair)

cd <pack dir>  # backend modules resolve via process cwd
python scripts/spike/qwen_gguf_probe.py ... --device cuda --cell windows-x64-cuda --json-out docs/performance/evidence/qwen-gguf-windows-x64-cuda-<variant>.json

cd <pack dir>  # backend modules resolve via process cwd
python <repo>/scripts/spike/qwen_gguf_probe.py --profile <base|customvoice> --quantization <Q8_0|Q4_K_M> --library ./libqwen.so --talker <models>/qwen-talker-0.6b-<profile>-<quant>.gguf --tokenizer <models>/qwen-tokenizer-12hz-<quant>.gguf (--speaker ryan | --ref-audio freeman.wav --ref-text <transcript>) --check-cancel --cell linux-x64-cpu --json-out <repo>/docs/performance/evidence/qwen-gguf-linux-x64-cpu-<profile>-<quant>.json

cd <pack dir>  # backend modules resolve via process cwd
python scripts/spike/qwen_gguf_probe.py ... --device cuda --cell linux-x64-cuda --json-out docs/performance/evidence/qwen-gguf-linux-x64-cuda-<variant>.json

cd <pack dir>  # backend modules resolve via process cwd
python scripts/spike/qwen_gguf_probe.py ... --device cpu --cell macos-arm64-cpu --json-out docs/performance/evidence/qwen-gguf-macos-arm64-cpu-<variant>.json

cd <pack dir>  # backend modules resolve via process cwd
python scripts/spike/qwen_gguf_probe.py ... --device metal --cell macos-arm64-metal --json-out docs/performance/evidence/qwen-gguf-macos-arm64-metal-<variant>.json

ggufMetadataEvidence.method: HTTP Range reads of the GGUF headers at the pinned revision; KV section only, no tensor data
notes: Speaker names are lowercase in the GGUF table; the prompt builder lowercases input before lookup, so the app's 'Uncle_Fu' casing resolves to 'uncle_fu'.
Speaker dialects apply only when the requested language is chinese or auto; the ABI does not expose dialect entries, so dialect evidence lives here and in qt_synthesize behavior.

Base talkers carry 10 language rows (no dialect entries) — confirmed by qt_language_name enumeration on the real Q4_K_M base model; custom_voice carries 12. 'auto' is accepted by qt_synthesize but is not a table entry.
Tokenizer GGUFs carry general.architecture=qwen3-tts-tokenizer and general.file_type but no model_type; pairing is by quantization (file_type) per the spec.
